original_question: If a Banach algebra A is approximately amenable, meaning that every continuous derivation from A into the dual of any Banach A-bimodule is approximately inner, must A also be pseudo-amenable, meaning that A has an approximate diagonal (u_i) in the projective tensor product A \hat{\otimes} A such that a u_i - u_i a -> 0 and \u03c0(u_i)a -> a for all a in A?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Question 3: "Does approximate amenability imply pseudo-amenability?" This is the paper’s nearest official formulation of your draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact implication the paper asks about: whether approximate amenability of a Banach algebra A forces pseudo-amenability of the same algebra A. It also uses the right ambient notions: approximate amenability is defined via approximate innerness of every continuous derivation D:A→X* for every Banach A-bimodule X, and pseudo-amenability is defined via an approximate diagonal in the projective tensor product. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
missing_details: The paper states this as an open question ('Question 3'), not as a theorem or established implication. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should specify that approximate innerness is in the norm topology of X*, for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D:A→X*. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

The pseudo-amenability side should explicitly mention that the approximate diagonal is a net in the projective tensor product A \widehat{\otimes} A and is not required to be bounded. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

The nearby official context is important: Theorem 2.6(1) gives only that A is approximately amenable if and only if the unitization A^# is pseudo-amenable, so Question 3 asks whether one can remove the passage to A^#. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

The paper also records a positive case that your draft omits: the implication is known to hold if A has a central approximate identity, in particular if A is abelian. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Another paper-faithful hidden point is the approximate-identity obstruction: every pseudo-amenable Banach algebra has a two-sided approximate identity, whereas for approximately amenable algebras the paper only states existence of left and right approximate identities in general; hence an approximately amenable algebra without a two-sided approximate identity would be a counterexample. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

Theorem 2.7(1) supplies a further nearby restriction: if A has a bounded approximate identity, then approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability are already equivalent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
refined_question: Let A be a Banach algebra. Suppose A is approximately amenable, in the sense that for every Banach A-bimodule X, every continuous derivation D:A→X* is approximately inner in norm. Must A itself be pseudo-amenable; equivalently, must there exist a (not necessarily bounded) net (u_i) in the projective tensor product A \widehat{\otimes} A such that a·u_i-u_i·a→0 and π_A(u_i)a→a for every a∈A? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
justification: The draft is already very close, but the paper’s exact target is the official open problem in Section 2 labeled Question 3, not a broader variant. Definitions 1.2 and 1.3 provide the precise meanings of 'approximately amenable' and 'pseudo-amenable'. The neighboring results explain the intended sharpness: Theorem 2.6(1) shows that approximate amenability of A is equivalent to pseudo-amenability of the unitization A^#, while Theorem 2.7(1) shows that the desired implication is already true when A has a bounded approximate identity. Section 3.1 then highlights why Question 3 is delicate: pseudo-amenability gives a two-sided approximate identity, but approximate amenability is only known in general to give left and right approximate identities separately. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
